skill.name: tasknotes
skill.description: Manage Obsidian TaskNotes tasks through the local plugin API for listing, creating, updating, deleting, statistics, and options.
skill.summary: Create, list, update, and delete TaskNotes tasks in Obsidian through the local HTTP API.
skill.author: ArtemXTech

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs local CLI commands and uses the TaskNotes localhost HTTP API to read, create, update, and delete Obsidian tasks. No prompt injection or external cloud endpoint was found, but the skill handles an API token, loads a vault-root .env file, and has mutating and destructive task operations.

remediation.issue: API port value is not validated before URL construction.
remediation.suggestion: Parse TASKNOTES_API_PORT as an integer from 1 to 65535 and reject values containing URL metacharacters before building BASE_URL.

remediation.issue: The script loads a vault-root .env file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a skill-specific config file or read only explicit process variables, and document that unrelated secrets should not be placed in that .env file.

remediation.issue: Delete operations have no built-in confirmation or dry run.
remediation.suggestion: Require a --force flag, add a confirmation prompt for interactive use, or prefer archive behavior when the TaskNotes API supports it.

remediation.issue: The skill documents mutating shell commands for agents.
remediation.suggestion: State that create, update, and delete commands should be confirmed by the user before execution in agent workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated API Port Can Redirect Authenticated Requests
semantic_findings.description: TASKNOTES_API_PORT is inserted into BASE_URL without numeric validation, and TASKNOTES_API_KEY is sent as a bearer header. A crafted port value could change URL parsing and send task data or the token away from localhost.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly interpolates API_PORT into an HTTP URL and sends headers through requests. Exploitation requires malicious environment or config control, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Task Deletion Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The CLI exposes a delete command that calls DELETE /tasks/{id} without an in-script confirmation, dry-run, or soft-delete safeguard. A mistaken task path can remove a TaskNotes task from the vault.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented delete command maps directly to a DELETE API request in code. No confirmation or recovery safeguard is visible in the cited lines.

content.value_statement: Obsidian task management can be slow when tasks live behind plugin screens. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code manage TaskNotes through the local API.
actual_capabilities: List TaskNotes tasks with filters for status, project, priority, overdue state, and result limit.
Create tasks with title, project, priority, status, dates, contexts, estimates, and details.
Update existing tasks by file path with new status, priority, title, dates, or details.
Delete TaskNotes tasks through the local TaskNotes API.
Show task statistics and available projects, statuses, and priorities.
Return human-readable tables or structured output for agent workflows.
limitations: Requires Obsidian with the TaskNotes HTTP API enabled and reachable on localhost.
Can only use fields and filters exposed by the TaskNotes plugin API.
Create, update, and delete actions can change local task notes.
Authentication depends on a local API token stored outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Review Daily Tasks
use_cases.description: List active or overdue TaskNotes items before planning the workday.

use_cases.title: Capture Project Work
use_cases.description: Create linked tasks with priority, schedule, context, and project metadata.

use_cases.title: Automate Task Updates
use_cases.description: Let an agent mark completed work, update details, or pull task statistics after a session.

prompt_templates.title: List Current Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my open TaskNotes tasks. Limit the result to 10 items and use a readable table.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TaskNotes task titled "Prepare release notes" for the Website Redesign project with high priority.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Project Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: List TaskNotes tasks for the Website Redesign project, grouped by status, and include due dates when available.

prompt_templates.title: Update After Work Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Find in-progress TaskNotes items for Website Redesign. Ask before changing anything, then mark selected completed tasks as done.

output_examples.input: Show in-progress tasks for Website Redesign.
output_examples.output: A concise table with task titles, statuses, priorities, due dates, and project links.

output_examples.input: Create a high priority task for release notes.
output_examples.output: A confirmation with the created task title, path, status, and priority.

output_examples.input: What TaskNotes options can I use?
output_examples.output: A readable list of configured projects, statuses, and priorities from the local plugin.

best_practices: Run the options command first to confirm valid status and priority names.
Use an API token for the local TaskNotes API and store only required variables.
Confirm task file paths before update or delete operations.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when Obsidian or the TaskNotes HTTP API is closed.
Do not store unrelated secrets in the vault root .env file.
Do not delete tasks by guessed file paths.

faq.question: Does this skill require Obsidian?
faq.answer: Yes. Obsidian must be running with the TaskNotes plugin and HTTP API enabled.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create and update tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create tasks and update status, priority, title, due dates, scheduled dates, and details.

faq.question: Can it delete tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can call the TaskNotes delete endpoint, so confirm the task path first.

faq.question: Where does the API token come from?
faq.answer: The script reads TASKNOTES_API_KEY from the vault root .env file or the process environment.

faq.question: Does it send data to a cloud service?
faq.answer: No cloud endpoint is shown. The code targets a localhost TaskNotes API, but the port value should be validated.
